questions.scenario: During the post-pour stripping of formwork for a heavily loaded core-wall basement element, the RGBC site team discovers extensive honeycombing and voiding across a 3m x 2m section where reinforcement is completely exposed. The Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) orally instructs the RGBC site agent to immediately patch the voids with structural epoxy mortar before the Building Authority's site inspection.
options: A. The RGBC can lawfully execute the verbal instruction immediately, provided the patch repair mortar complies with the approved material specifications.

B. Under Section 9(5)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance, the RGBC has a mandatory duty to notify the Building Authority and the AP/RSE in writing of such structural defect before taking unauthorized remedial action.
C. The RGBC must only notify the Authorized Person (AP), as notification to the Building Authority is solely the statutory responsibility of the RSE under Section 9(3).
D. The RGBC is legally required to conceal the honeycombing immediately under Section 9(5)(a) to protect the exposed rebar from rapid atmospheric corrosion.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 9(5)(b) & Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Section 9(5)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance mandates that an RGBC shall give written notice to the Building Authority and to the AP/RSE/RGE of any defect in the building or building works that may affect safety. Carrying out unapproved repairs to conceal major structural defects without written notification constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A). Complying with verbal instructions does not exonerate the RGBC from its statutory obligation.

questions.scenario: When granting consent for the construction of rock-socketed steel H-piles under Section 16(1)(b), the Building Authority imposes conditions under Section 17(1)(a) requiring proof drilling 5 metres into sound bedrock for 100% of the piles. Due to tight handover schedules and drilling rig breakdowns, the RGBC completes proof drilling to only 3 metres for five piles and proceeds to cast the pile caps without the Building Authority's prior written waiver.
options: A. The RGBC commits no criminal offence, as Section 17 conditions are technical guidelines that can be varied with the sole written consent of the project RSE.
B. The RGBC has only committed a civil breach of contract with the developer, provided the pile caps pass non-destructive sonic integrity testing.

C. Under Section 40(2AA) of the Buildings Ordinance, failing to comply with any condition imposed by the Building Authority under Section 17(1) is a criminal offence punishable by a fine at Level 6 ($100,000) and 2 years imprisonment.
D. The RGBC can retrospectively legalize the omitted drilling depth by submitting an indemnity bond together with the Form BA14 application.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 17(1)(a) & Section 40(2AA)
questions.rationale: Section 17(1)(a) of Cap. 123 empowers the Building Authority to impose conditions when granting consent for foundation or ground works. Under Section 40(2AA), any person who fails to comply with any condition imposed under Section 17(1) commits an offence and is liable upon conviction to a fine at Level 6 ($100,000) and imprisonment for 2 years. An RSE has no statutory authority to relax a Section 17 condition imposed by the Building Authority.

questions.scenario: An RGBC commenced foundation works pursuant to a valid consent issued under Section 16(1)(b). Due to a protracted contractual and financial dispute between the developer and the main contractor, all physical works on site ceased completely on 5 February 2024. As of 10 June 2024, the dispute is resolved and the contractor prepares to immediately resume piling without notifying the Buildings Department.
options: A. The consent is deemed revoked under Section 20(1) because works were suspended for more than 3 months; the RGBC cannot resume works until an application for renewal is granted under Section 20(2).
B. The RGBC may resume works immediately without formality, as an active consent remains valid for 24 months regardless of any intermediate site suspension.
C. The RGBC only needs to serve a fresh 7-day commencement notice on Form BA10 under B(A)R Regulation 20(1), without needing a Section 20(2) renewal.
D. The RGBC must surrender the registration certificate under Section 13 because site suspension for over 90 days triggers automatic deregistration.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & (2); B(A)R Regulation 34 & Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, consent is deemed revoked if the building works, once commenced, are suspended for a period of more than 3 months. To resume works, an application for renewal of consent must be submitted to the Building Authority under Section 20(2) on Form BA9 in accordance with B(A)R Regulation 34. Resuming works under a revoked consent is illegal under Section 14(1) and constitutes an offence under Section 40(1AA)/40(2A).

questions.scenario: Upon practical completion of an 18-storey commercial development, the AP submits Form BA13 applying for an Occupation Permit under Section 21(1). During the pre-OP joint inspection, the Building Authority discovers that the main underground foul drainage network has not been connected to the public sewer as depicted on the approved drainage plans, and untreated wastewater is discharging into an open storm drain.
options: A. The Building Authority must issue a full Occupation Permit because the main superstructure is structurally complete and safe.
B. The Building Authority may only issue a Cease Works Order under Section 23, but has no power to withhold the Occupation Permit once BA13 is accepted.
C. The Building Authority can only refuse the OP if the Authorized Person specifically requests an adjournment in writing.

D. Under Section 21(6)(d) of the Buildings Ordinance, the Building Authority is statutorily empowered to refuse to issue the Occupation Permit because the drainage work has not been completed in accordance with approved plans.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 21(6)(d)
questions.rationale: Section 21(6)(d) of Cap. 123 specifically empowers the Building Authority to refuse to issue an Occupation Permit or Temporary Occupation Permit if any drainage work has not been completed or connection to a public sewer has not been made in accordance with the regulations or approved plans. Discharging foul effluent into an open storm drain is a direct ground for statutory refusal under s.21(6)(d) and s.21(6)(a).

questions.scenario: Following an excessive ground settlement reading of 45mm and cracking on an adjacent public highway during bulk excavation, the Building Authority serves an immediate Cease Works Order under Section 23(1) of the Buildings Ordinance on the RGBC. To prevent his rented hydraulic excavators from sitting idle, the RGBC Authorized Signatory directs the site team to continue benching down excavation in the center of the site.
options: A. Continuing excavation is lawful provided the works are conducted more than 10 metres away from the site boundary where settlement occurred.

B. Failing to comply with an order to cease works under Section 23(1) is an offence under Section 40(2C), carrying a fine of HK$50,000 and 1 year imprisonment, plus a daily fine for each day the offence continues.
C. The RGBC can legally ignore the Section 23(1) order if the project Registered Geotechnical Engineer (RGE) countersigns an internal risk assessment.
D. An order under Section 23(1) only applies to the Authorized Person; the RGBC cannot be held liable for carrying out works instructed by the developer.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 23(1), (2) & Section 40(2C)
questions.rationale: Under Section 23(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, the Building Authority may order the cessation of building works if they are being carried out in a dangerous manner or causing danger. Under Section 23(2), no person shall carry out any building works contrary to such an order. Section 40(2C) provides that any person who contravenes Section 23(2) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of $50,000 and imprisonment for 1 year, plus a daily fine of $5,000 for each day of continuing contravention.

questions.scenario: During major unauthorized structural alterations inside an occupied multi-tenant industrial building, an RGBC's workers remove three critical reinforced concrete columns at ground floor, resulting in extensive diagonal shear cracking on upper floor slabs and immediate danger of progressive structural collapse. The Building Authority determines that all occupants must be evacuated immediately to prevent loss of life.
options: A. The Building Authority must first issue a standard 30-day Demolition Order under Section 24(1) and wait for the statutory appeal period to expire before vacating anyone.
B. The RGBC Authorized Signatory has the sole statutory authority under Section 9(5) to declare the premises closed and deploy private security to evict tenants.

C. The Building Authority may apply to the District Court or a Magistrate under Section 24A (or exercise emergency powers under Section 24B) for a Closure Order to close the building and secure its immediate evacuation.
D. The Building Authority must refer the matter to the Fire Services Department, as the Buildings Department has no statutory authority to close buildings.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 24A & Section 24B
questions.rationale: Section 24A and Section 24B of the Buildings Ordinance empower the Building Authority to apply for and obtain Closure Orders from the court (or make emergency closure orders under s.24B when danger is imminent) to close buildings that are dangerous or liable to become dangerous, evicting all occupants immediately to protect public safety. Section 24 is an order for demolition/alteration of unauthorized building works, not an emergency closure order.

questions.scenario: To avoid critical path delay during the casting of transfer girders, an RGBC Authorized Signatory knowingly signs and submits a Form BA14 completion declaration to the Building Authority stating that all reinforcement couplers underwent full tensile and elongation testing by a HOKLAS laboratory. In reality, no laboratory testing was ever commissioned, and the mill test sheets submitted were fabricated in the site office.
options: A. Under Section 40(1AA) of the Buildings Ordinance, knowingly making any false representation or false statement in any document submitted to the Building Authority is a serious offence punishable by a fine of HK$1,000,000 and 3 years imprisonment.
B. The RGBC can only be subject to an administrative warning under PNAP APP-21, as mill certificates are not statutory forms prescribed under Cap. 123.
C. The maximum penalty is limited to a Level 4 fine ($25,000) under the Summary Offences Ordinance because the concrete was already cast.
D. Criminal liability under Section 40(1AA) falls exclusively on the Registered Structural Engineer who specifies the coupler performance standards.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 40(1AA)
questions.rationale: Section 40(1AA) of Cap. 123 provides that any person who knowingly makes any false representation or false statement in any plan, certificate, form or other document submitted to the Building Authority under the Buildings Ordinance commits an offence. The statutory penalty is a fine of HK$1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years. Submitting fabricated test reports or false declarations on statutory forms (like Form BA14) triggers direct liability under this section.

questions.scenario: An RGBC modifies the shoring configuration of an excavation and lateral support (ELS) scheme without seeking prior approval or amendment from the Building Authority. The modified shoring proves severely under-designed, resulting in sudden bucking of the steel struts, total collapse of the contiguous pile wall, and severe crushing injuries to two workers inside the pit.
options: A. The RGBC can only be charged with a minor procedural contravention under B(A)R Regulation 10 for failing to keep records on site.

B. Under Section 40(2B)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance, carrying out building works in a manner that causes injury to any person or damage to any property is an offence carrying a fine of HK$1,000,000 and 3 years imprisonment.
C. Since the collapse occurred on private land, only the Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance applies, excluding Cap. 123 liability.
D. The RGBC is completely immune from Buildings Ordinance criminal prosecution if the AP failed to supervise the site that day under Section 4(3).
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 40(2B)(b)
questions.rationale: Section 40(2B)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance provides that any person directly concerned with the carrying out of any building works who carries out such works in a manner that causes injury to any person or damage to any property commits an offence. The prescribed penalty on conviction is a fine of HK$1,000,000 and imprisonment for 3 years. This applies concurrently with labor safety legislation (FIUO) and operates independently of divergence offences under s.40(2A).

questions.scenario: Following an RGBC's conviction under Section 40(2A) for carrying out structural works with gross material divergence from approved plans, the Building Authority refers the contractor to a Disciplinary Board appointed under Section 5(3A) of the Buildings Ordinance. The Disciplinary Board conducts a formal hearing under Section 13.
options: A. The Disciplinary Board has the statutory power to sentence the RGBC Authorized Signatory to 6 months of custodial imprisonment.
B. The Disciplinary Board may only impose a formal reprimand and cannot levy any financial penalties or remove the contractor from the register.

C. Under Section 13(4), the Disciplinary Board may order the RGBC to be removed from the register permanently or for a specified period, fine the contractor up to HK$250,000, or issue a reprimand, but cannot impose custodial sentences.
D. The Disciplinary Board is legally required to refer the case to the Hong Kong Police Force to determine the contractor's professional registration status.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 13(4) & (4A)
questions.rationale: Under Section 13(4) of the Buildings Ordinance, a Disciplinary Board, upon finding a registered contractor guilty of misconduct or negligence, may order that the name of the contractor be removed from the register (either permanently or for such period as the board thinks fit), order a fine not exceeding HK$250,000, or reprimand the contractor, and make orders as to costs. Disciplinary Boards are quasi-judicial administrative tribunals and have NO custodial sentencing powers (imprisonment can only be imposed by the criminal courts).

questions.scenario: A shipment of high-strength structural steel I-sections arrives on site lacking the required mill certificates and CE/GB markings specified in the approved structural drawings. Due to project liquidating damages, the RGBC AS directs his fabrication team to immediately weld and erect these steel sections as roof transfer trusses before any material test results are obtained.
options: A. Under Section 9(5)(c) of the Buildings Ordinance, the RGBC is under an explicit statutory duty to secure that the materials used are in accordance with the Ordinance and approved plans; using unverified materials contravenes this duty and constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A)(c).
B. The RGBC's actions are fully compliant under Section 17, provided the structural steel undergoes post-installation ultrasonic testing after full roof completion.
C. The duty of ensuring material fitness rests exclusively on the Registered Structural Engineer; the RGBC is merely a labour supplier with no material obligations under Section 9.
D. Section 9(5)(c) only applies to concrete works; structural steelwork is exempt from statutory material verification under the Code of Practice for Structural Use of Steel.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 9(5)(c) & Section 40(2A)(c)
questions.rationale: Section 9(5)(c) of the Buildings Ordinance explicitly mandates that a Registered General Building Contractor shall 'secure that the materials used in the building works or street works are in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance and the approved plans'. Furthermore, under Section 40(2A)(c), any registered contractor who uses any materials which do not comply with the provisions of the Ordinance commits a criminal offence liable to a fine of HK$1,000,000 and 3 years imprisonment.

questions.scenario: A registered main contractor executing a residential development enters into liquidation during superstructure construction. The project owner immediately terminates the contract and engages a new Registered General Building Contractor (RGBC) to take over the partially completed building works. Before executing any physical works on site, what is the mandatory statutory notification and procedure required from the newly appointed RGBC and the owner?
options: A. The owner and the newly appointed RGBC must submit Form BA8 (Notice of Appointment) to the Building Authority within 7 days of the appointment under Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1), and obtain a formal written re-consent from the Building Authority before resuming works.

B. The owner and the newly appointed RGBC must submit Form BA8 within 7 days of the appointment pursuant to Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1), and ensure the Authorized Person confirms site safety compliance before physical work resumes under the existing valid consent.

C. The incoming RGBC must submit a fresh Form BA10 notice of commencement directly to the Building Authority at least 14 days prior to taking over the site, which automatically supersedes the outgoing contractor's Form BA8.

D. The outgoing contractor must submit Form BA14 for the partially completed works within 7 days, failing which the incoming RGBC cannot submit Form BA8 under Building (Administration) Regulation 8(2).
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1) & (2); Form BA8
questions.rationale: Under Building (Administration) Regulation 8(1), every person for whom building works are being carried out must notify the Building Authority (BA) of the appointment of a registered contractor on the specified form (Form BA8) within 7 days of such appointment. Under B(A)R 8(2), notice must also be given within 7 days when a contractor ceases to be appointed. Works can continue under the existing valid consent once the AP coordinates the handover and statutory notifications are lodged; a brand-new consent is not required simply due to contractor replacement unless consent has lapsed under BO Section 20(1).

questions.scenario: An RGBC obtained formal consent to commence foundation works for a commercial tower on 1 March. Due to financing negotiations between the developer and lenders, physical construction on site did not commence, and the site remained completely idle until 15 June (over 3 months later). The developer now instructs the RGBC to mobilize heavy piling rigs and commence bored piling immediately.
options: A. The RGBC can mobilize immediately provided a revised Form BA10 is submitted 7 days prior to piling, because the original consent remains valid for 12 months.

B. Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance, the consent is deemed revoked as works did not commence within 3 months; the RGBC must apply for and obtain renewal of consent via Form BA9 under BO Section 20(2) and B(A)R Regulation 34 before commencing.
C. Under Building (Administration) Regulation 27, the consent was automatically suspended and can be reactivated simply by lodging a site safety plan addendum signed by the RGBC Authorized Signatory.
D. The RGBC may proceed under Section 16(1)(b) of the Buildings Ordinance if the Authorized Person issues an administrative letter granting a 60-day extension to the commencement window.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 20(1) & 20(2); B(A)R Regulation 34; Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 20(1), a consent given by the Building Authority is deemed revoked if the building works are not commenced within 3 months from the date of the consent. Former B(A)R Regulation 27 was repealed; renewal is governed by BO Section 20(2) and B(A)R Regulation 34 using Form BA9. Commencing works on site after the 3-month lapse without obtaining renewal under Section 20(2) constitutes carrying out building works without consent under BO Section 14(1), an offence punishable under Section 40(1AA) or 40(2A).

questions.scenario: The Building Authority issues formal consent for superstructure construction on Monday, 5 August. An aggressive developer orders the RGBC to start structural column casting on Friday, 9 August. The RGBC's Authorized Signatory signs and submits Form BA10 (Notice of Commencement) to the Buildings Department on Tuesday, 6 August. What is the legal consequence if the RGBC starts works on 9 August as directed?
options: A. The commencement is legal because consent has already been granted and Form BA10 was served before casting commenced.

B. The commencement is unlawful under Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1), which strictly requires Form BA10 to be submitted at least 7 days before the date on which works commence; early commencement constitutes an offence under BO Section 40(2A).
C. The commencement is deemed accepted under B(A)R Regulation 20(2) provided the Registered Structural Engineer was physically on site during the column pour.

D. The RGBC incurs no liability because the statutory 7-day notice period under B(A)R Regulation 20(1) is an administrative guideline that applies only to the Authorized Person, not the registered contractor.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1); Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A); Form BA10
questions.rationale: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) requires that notice in the specified form (Form BA10) shall be given to the Building Authority of the date on which works are to be commenced at least 7 days before that date. Both the AP/RSE and RGBC must sign Form BA10. Starting works on 9 August (only 3 days after submission) violates B(A)R 20(1) and exposes the RGBC and its Authorized Signatory to prosecution under BO Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: A 35-storey mixed-use building achieves practical completion. The works included both general building works executed by the RGBC and specialized ventilation works executed by a Registered Specialist Contractor (Ventilation Works Category). Before the Authorized Person can submit Form BA12 to apply for an Occupation Permit under Section 21 of the Buildings Ordinance, which completion forms must be formally executed?
options: A. The RGBC alone executes Form BA14 covering all works, including the mechanical ventilation system, pursuant to B(A)R Regulation 25(1).

B. The RGBC executes Form BA14 under B(A)R Regulation 25(1), while the Registered Specialist Contractor (Ventilation) must independently execute Form BA14A under B(A)R Regulation 25(2) certifying completion in accordance with approved plans.
C. The Registered Specialist Contractor executes Form BA14, whereas the RGBC submits Form BA13 for a temporary permit.
D. Only Form BA12 signed by the AP and owner is required; Forms BA14 and BA14A are internal Buildings Department audit records submitted 28 days after the Occupation Permit is granted.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 25(1) & (2); Form BA12, BA14, BA14A; BO Section 21
questions.rationale: Under B(A)R Regulation 25(1), the RGBC must certify on Form BA14 that the building works have been carried out in accordance with the Buildings Ordinance and approved plans. Under B(A)R Regulation 25(2), where specialized works (such as ventilation systems) are carried out by a Registered Specialist Contractor, the RSC must execute Form BA14A. Both certificates are essential prerequisites supporting the AP's application for an Occupation Permit under BO Section 21 via Form BA12.

questions.scenario: An RGBC completes the podium levels (Floors G–4, intended for shopping mall and carpark use) of a twin-tower development, while the residential superstructure of Floors 5–40 is still undergoing internal architectural and wet trades. The developer wishes to open the retail podium to the public immediately. Which statutory procedure must the project team follow?
options: A. The AP must submit Form BA13 to apply for a Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) under BO Section 21(2), supported by the RGBC's Form BA14 certifying practical completion of the podium works.
B. The RGBC can issue a partial handover letter to the developer under PNAP APP-21, allowing public occupation without BD involvement until all 40 storeys are complete.
C. The developer must apply for a full Occupation Permit on Form BA12, because the Buildings Ordinance does not permit occupation of a building part-by-part.
D. The AP and RGBC must convert the remaining unfinished residential floors into Class I Minor Works using Form MW01 so the podium can receive an immediate permanent OP.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123) Section 21(2); Building (Administration) Regulation 25; Form BA13 & Form BA14
questions.rationale: Under BO Section 21(2), the Building Authority may issue a temporary occupation permit (TOP) for part of a new building that has been completed to the BA's satisfaction. The AP applies on specified Form BA13, supported by the RGBC's Form BA14 certifying that the relevant podium works have been completed in compliance with the approved plans and statutory regulations.

questions.scenario: A building owner appoints an RGBC to carry out Class I Minor Works (Item 1.1: alteration of an existing external wall opening exceeding 1.5m in height). The owner also engages a Prescribed Building Professional (PBP/AP). Under the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), which sequence of statutory forms must be submitted to the Building Authority?
options: A. Form MW03 at least 7 days before commencement, followed by Form MW04 within 14 days after completion.
B. Form MW01 together with prescribed plans at least 7 days prior to commencement, followed by Form MW02 together with record photos within 14 days after completion.
C. Form MW05 within 14 days after completion; no prior notice or plan submission is required for Class I works.
D. Form BA10 at least 7 days prior to commencement, followed by Form BA14 within 28 days after completion.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 27 & 28; Forms MW01 & MW02
questions.rationale: For Class I minor works, B(MW)R Section 27 requires the PBP to submit notice of commencement on Form MW01 accompanied by prescribed plans at least 7 days before commencing the works. Following completion, B(MW)R Section 28 requires the PBP and PRC (RGBC) to submit a completion certificate on Form MW02 with photographs within 14 days after completion. Forms MW03/MW04 are for Class II works, and Form MW05 is for Class III works.

questions.scenario: A corporate client engages an RGBC to carry out Class II Minor Works (Item 2.13: erection of supporting frames for air-conditioning units projecting between 0.6m and 1.5m from an external wall). No Prescribed Building Professional (AP/RSE) is engaged, as none is required for this specific Class II item. Which forms and timelines apply to the RGBC under B(MW)R (Cap. 123N)?
options: A. Submit Form MW01 at least 14 days before commencement and Form MW02 within 7 days after completion.
B. Submit Form MW03 at least 7 days before commencement, and Form MW06 within 14 days after completion.
C. Submit Form MW03 at least 7 days before commencement, and Form MW04 within 14 days after completion.
D. Submit Form MW05 within 14 days after completion, with no prior notice required.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Sections 30 & 32; Forms MW03 & MW06
questions.rationale: For Class II minor works where no Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) is appointed, notice of commencement must be submitted by the Prescribed Registered Contractor on Form MW03 at least 7 days before commencement under B(MW)R Section 30. Upon completion, the contractor must submit Form MW06 (Certificate of completion for Class II works where NO PBP is appointed) within 14 days after completion under B(MW)R Section 32. Form MW04 is strictly reserved for Class II works where a PBP has been appointed.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is engaged to install a small metal drying rack projecting not more than 750mm from an external wall in a domestic unit (a designated Class III Minor Works item under Schedule 1 of Cap. 123N). The contractor's junior engineer prepares to submit a notice of commencement on Form MW03 to the Buildings Department 7 days before starting. What should the RGBC Authorized Signatory advise?
options: A. Approve the submission, as all minor works classes strictly require 7 days advance notice under the Building (Minor Works) Regulation.

B. Reject the Form MW03 submission, because Class III minor works require no prior commencement notice; under B(MW)R Section 35, the RGBC must instead submit Form MW05 together with before-and-after photographs within 14 days after completion.
C. Upgrade the filing to Form MW01 accompanied by structural calculations, because external wall fixtures must always be certified by a Registered Structural Engineer.
D. Advise that drying racks are classified as exempted works under BO Section 41(3) and therefore no Buildings Department forms whatsoever are legally permitted to be lodged.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 35; Form MW05
questions.rationale: Under B(MW)R Section 35, Class III minor works do not require any prior notification to the Building Authority before commencement. The statutory requirement is solely post-completion: the PRC (or RGBC) must submit Form MW05 together with photographs taken before and after the works within 14 days after completing the works. Submitting Form MW03 is incorrect and unnecessary for Class III works.

questions.scenario: Under the Minor Works Control System (Cap. 123N), a shopping mall manager hires an RGBC to carry out internal alteration works involving the removal of non-loadbearing masonry partitions. The manager also voluntarily appoints an Authorized Person (AP) as a Prescribed Building Professional to supervise the works, which fall under Class II minor works. Upon physical completion of the works, which form must be submitted to the Building Authority?
options: A. Form MW06 signed solely by the RGBC's Authorized Signatory under B(MW)R Section 32.
B. Form MW04 signed by both the appointed Prescribed Building Professional (AP) and the RGBC's Authorized Signatory under B(MW)R Section 31.
C. Form BA14 submitted under Building (Administration) Regulation 25(1).
D. Form MW02 accompanied by certified structural drawings under B(MW)R Section 28.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Section 31; Form MW04
questions.rationale: Under B(MW)R Section 31, when a Prescribed Building Professional (PBP) is appointed for Class II minor works (whether mandatory or voluntary), the certificate of completion must be submitted on Form MW04, signed by both the PBP and the PRC (RGBC). Form MW06 is used under Section 32 ONLY when NO Prescribed Building Professional is appointed for Class II works.

questions.scenario: A retail tenant requests an RGBC to construct an opening of 3m x 2.5m through an existing 300mm thick reinforced concrete structural transfer plate to accommodate a new escalator. The tenant insists this should be expedited under the Minor Works Control System as a Class I Minor Works item using Form MW01. How must the RGBC Authorized Signatory respond?
options: A. Accept the instruction and submit Form MW01 with structural strengthening details prepared by a Registered Structural Engineer, since Class I covers all structural slab alterations.

B. Refuse to execute the works under the Minor Works Control System, because forming an opening in a structural transfer plate or major structural loadbearing element exceeds the statutory limits of Cap. 123N Schedule 1 and requires formal plan approval and consent under BO Section 14(1).
C. Treat the works as Class II minor works under Form MW03, provided temporary steel props are certified under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision.
D. Submit Form BA9 to the Building Authority requesting a waiver of formal plan approval pursuant to Section 42 of the Buildings Ordinance.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N) Schedule 1; Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1) & Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under Schedule 1 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation (Cap. 123N), slab opening items (such as Item 1.13) strictly apply only to ordinary floor slabs not involving prestressed elements, transfer plates, cantilevers, or beams, and have strict dimensional/area limits (e.g. area not exceeding 4.5m2 and not cutting main structural framing members). Cutting into a structural transfer plate is fundamentally outside the Minor Works regime. Proceeding under MWCS without formal plan approval and consent under BO Section 14(1) is an illegal act subject to criminal prosecution under Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: During a routine audit by the Buildings Department (BD) on an active 28-storey superstructure site, BD officers demand immediate inspection of the approved structural plans, the supervision plan, and the approved drainage plans. The RGBC's site agent can only present electronic copies on a tablet and explains that all stamped hard copies are kept safely at the contractor's head office to prevent them from being soiled or damaged. No approved hard-copy plans are available on site.
options: A. The RGBC has complied with the statutory intent provided that identical soft copies can be displayed and printed immediately upon request.
B. The RGBC is in breach of Building (Administration) Regulation 10, as stamped approved plans and supervision plans must be continuously kept on the site of works.
C. The RGBC is exempt from keeping structural plans on site once the Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) has endorsed the digital contractor's quality plan.
D. The RGBC is only required to maintain the safety supervision plan on site; approved structural and drainage drawings are only required at the AP's registered office.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 10 & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2B)
questions.rationale: Under Regulation 10 of the Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A), the registered contractor carrying out building works must keep on the site of such works: (a) approved plans and any documents issued by the Building Authority; and (b) a copy of the supervision plan. Keeping them exclusively at the head office or in digital format without explicit BD approval is a statutory contravention under B(A)R Reg. 10 and attracts penal liability under BO Section 40(2B).

questions.scenario: Ten months after the issuance of the occupation permit for a residential tower, a major underground storm drain collapses near the basement perimeter wall. The Building Authority conducts a forensic investigation and issues a statutory requisition requiring the RGBC to furnish all concrete cube test certificates, mill certificates for reinforcement bars, and the contractor's TCP inspection logbooks. The RGBC's Authorized Signatory refuses to provide them, claiming the project was closed and company records were archived and shredded six months after handover.
options: A. The RGBC is legally safe because a contractor's retention duty ends immediately upon the issuance of the occupation permit under BO Section 21.
B. The RGBC is liable under Building (Administration) Regulation 11, which mandates retention of all test records and supervisory logs for not less than 12 months after work completion.
C. The RGBC is only required to retain mill test certificates for structural steelwork, while concrete cube and grout logs can be discarded after 90 days.
D. The duty to retain test records and supervisory documents rests exclusively with the Authorised Person (AP) and Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) under B(A)R Regulation 37.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 11 & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under Regulation 11 of the Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A), a registered contractor must keep and preserve all records of tests of materials, as well as supervisory logbooks required under the Ordinance or conditions of consent, for not less than 12 months from the date of completion of the building works. Destroying or failing to produce these records within the 12-month statutory period constitutes an offence under BO Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: An RGBC receives consent to commence site formation works from the Building Authority on Thursday, 2 October. To meet a critical contract milestone, the RGBC immediately submits the notice of intention to commence works (Form BA10) on Friday, 3 October, stating that mechanized earthworks and site formation will commence on Tuesday, 7 October (4 calendar days later).
options: A. The commencement notice is legally valid because 4 calendar days are sufficient when formal consent has already been granted under Section 16.
B. The RGBC may commence works provided the Authorized Signatory submits an indemnity letter along with Form BA10.
C. The commencement is invalid and unlawful because Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) requires at least 7 days' prior written notice on Form BA10 before commencing works.
D. The 7-day notice requirement applies only to superstructure works; site formation and demolition require only 48 hours' prior notification.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Administration) Regulation 20(1) & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2B)
questions.rationale: Under Regulation 20(1) of the Building (Administration) Regulations (Cap. 123A), a registered contractor must give to the Building Authority not less than 7 days' notice in writing on the specified form (Form BA10) of the date on which building works are to commence. Commencing works prior to the expiry of the mandatory 7-day statutory notice period constitutes a criminal offence under BO Section 40(2B).

questions.scenario: An RGBC was granted consent under Section 16(1)(b) to construct a two-level basement. Immediately after consent was issued, the client encountered severe financial difficulties, and no physical works commenced on site for four consecutive months. With fresh funding secured, the developer instructs the RGBC to immediately mobilize piling rigs and commence excavation on site under the original consent document.
options: A. The RGBC can mobilize immediately because an approved consent remains perpetually valid until formal revocation by the Building Authority under Section 24.

B. The RGBC cannot commence because under BO Section 20(1), the consent is deemed revoked if works are not commenced within 3 months, requiring a renewal application under BO Section 20(2) via Form BA9.
C. The RGBC only needs to re-submit Form BA10 with a revised 14-day notice period to automatically reactivate the dormant consent.
D. The RGBC must submit entirely fresh structural plans under BO Section 14(1) because plan approval lapses automatically after 90 days of inactivity.
questions.statutoryRef: Buildings Ordinance Section 20(1) & (2), B(A)R Regulation 34 & Form BA9
questions.rationale: Under Section 20(1) of the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), any consent given by the Building Authority to commence building works is deemed to be revoked if the works are not commenced within 3 months from the date of the consent, or if commenced, are suspended for a period of more than 3 months. To recommence, the contractor and AP must apply for a renewal of consent under Section 20(2) using Form BA9, and receive an endorsement under B(A)R Regulation 34 before any works can be carried out.

questions.scenario: An RGBC plans the erection of a temporary covered walkway adjoining an active commercial redevelopment on a public pavement. Due to site constraints including street furniture and a narrow curb, the RGBC designs the covered walkway with a clear internal pedestrian walking width of 0.95m and a minimum clear headroom of 2.1m. The RGBC submits this proposal as an emergency hoarding plan to BD.
options: A. The proposal violates PNRC 4 and B(P)R Reg 49, as covered walkways must maintain a minimum clear width of not less than 1.1m and a clear headroom of not less than 2.5m.
B. The proposal is acceptable provided overhead safety lighting of not less than 50 lux is installed throughout the walkway length.
C. The proposed dimensions are acceptable for urban pavements having an existing width of less than 1.5m under Appendix B of PNRC 4.
D. The proposal violates the clear width requirement of 1.5m, but satisfies the minimum headroom requirement of 2.0m under B(P)R Part IX.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 4 (Appendix A) & Building (Planning) Regulations Regulation 49
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 4 (APP-23 / PNRC 4) Appendix A and Building (Planning) Regulations Regulation 49, temporary covered walkways erected over or adjoining public thoroughfares must provide an unobstructed clear walkway width of not less than 1.1m (or match the existing pavement width if narrower, subject to approval) and must provide a minimum vertical clear headroom of not less than 2.5m throughout its length. The proposed 0.95m width and 2.1m headroom are strictly non-compliant.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is executing deep excavation and lateral support (ELS) works located 18 meters from an active underground railway tunnel in the Railway Protection Zone (RPZ). The monitoring plan approved by the Building Authority and MTR Corporation Limited (MTRCL) specifies an Alert Level of 20mm, an Alarm Level of 25mm, and an Action Level of 30mm for track settlement. During bulk excavation, an automated track settlement monitor registers a cumulative settlement of 21.2mm on the track bed.
options: A. The RGBC must immediately cease all construction works across the entire site and notify the Commissioner for Transport within 1 hour.
B. The RGBC may disregard the reading until the 25mm Alarm Level is breached, as Alert is merely an advisory internal threshold.
C. The RGBC must immediately review the construction methodology, step up monitoring frequency, notify the AP, RSE, BD, and MTRCL, and implement agreed mitigation measures pursuant to PNRC 14.
D. The RGBC must instruct its RPE geotechnical specialist to unilaterally raise the Alert Level to 25mm to avoid disrupting the project program.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 14 (PNAP APP-24) & Buildings Ordinance Section 17(1)
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 14 (Railway Protection), the 3-tier monitoring criteria (Alert, Alarm, Action) dictate specific procedural steps. When the Alert Level (typically 20mm track settlement or pre-agreed parameter) is reached or exceeded, the contractor must immediately notify the AP, RSE, BD, and MTRCL, review the construction methods and instrumentation data, step up monitoring frequency, and take preventive and mitigation measures. Total work stoppage is statutorily mandatory upon reaching the Action/Suspension Level, not the Alert Level.

questions.scenario: An RGBC is carrying out superstructure works on a 40-storey hotel development. The RGBC has only one approved Authorized Signatory (AS) on the Buildings Department register. Following an acute board dispute, the sole AS resigns with immediate effect and sends written notice to the Building Authority. The RGBC's Operations Director (a Registered Professional Engineer) directs the site team to continue casting the critical 5th floor transfer plate, promising to submit a replacement AS application within 14 days.
options: A. Concreting works can lawfully continue because the company holds a valid corporate registration as an RGBC under BO Section 8A.
B. Concreting works can continue provided the Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) undertakes continuous on-site supervision under Regulation 26.
C. All building works must cease immediately because under PNRC 38 and BO Section 9(5)/(6), an RGBC cannot lawfully execute building works without a designated Authorized Signatory.
D. Works may continue for an automatic 28-day statutory grace period while the replacement AS application is processed by the Contractors Registration Committee.
questions.statutoryRef: Practice Note for Registered Contractors PNRC 38 Section 4 & Buildings Ordinance Section 9(5), 9(6)
questions.rationale: Under PNRC 38 and the Buildings Ordinance, a corporate registered contractor must act through its approved Authorized Signatory (AS). If an RGBC has only one AS and that individual ceases to act, the contractor ceases to satisfy the registration requirements under Section 8B. Pursuant to PNRC 38, the contractor must immediately suspend all building works. Continuing works without an approved AS constitutes an illegal operation under BO Section 9(5) & 9(6), exposing the contractor and directors to prosecution under BO Section 40.

questions.scenario: During the construction of a reinforced concrete commercial podium, the RGBC encounters congested utility penetrations. To resolve the conflict, the RGBC and Registered Structural Engineer (RSE) decide to shift four primary structural transfer columns laterally by 600mm, alter the beam grid framing, and decrease the reinforcement ratio by 15% across the primary transfer girders. The RGBC plans to treat these design adjustments as 'Minor Amendments' to be submitted on completion via as-built drawings under PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52.
options: A. The changes fall squarely within the Minor Amendments framework because the gross floor area (GFA) and overall building height remain unaltered.

B. The RGBC is in breach of BO Section 14(1), as modifications to major structural elements, primary transfer members, and column layouts require formal prior plan approval and consent before execution.
C. Structural shifts up to 1,000mm in column positions are automatically deemed minor works under Schedule 1 of the Building (Minor Works) Regulation.
D. The contractor is protected from prosecution as long as the RSE signs a design certification on site prior to pouring concrete.
questions.statutoryRef: PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52 & Buildings Ordinance Section 14(1), Section 40(2A)
questions.rationale: Under PNAP APP-55 / PNRC 52, the minor amendment mechanism cannot be applied to significant changes affecting the structural integrity, major load-bearing elements, primary transfer girders, or alterations of the framing grid layout of major columns. Such works strictly require prior submission, formal structural plan approval, and consent under Section 14(1) of the Buildings Ordinance before execution. Proceeding without prior approval violates BO Section 14(1) and constitutes an offence under Section 40(2A).

questions.scenario: On a complex deep foundation and lateral support site, the Registered Geotechnical Engineer's (RGE) Stream TCP-T4 resigns abruptly. To avoid delaying the pile excavation, the RGBC's Authorized Signatory permits the RGBC's full-time site-based Contractor's Stream TCP-T4 (a qualified Registered Professional Engineer) to concurrently sign off both the Contractor's Stream and RGE Stream inspection logbooks for 14 days until a replacement is hired.
options: A. This concurrent appointment is permissible under the SSPS Code provided both streams require the same minimum academic qualification (T4 grade).

B. This concurrent appointment is strictly prohibited under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision, as TCPs in the Contractor's stream cannot simultaneously undertake supervisory duties in the AP/RSE/RGE streams.
C. This concurrent appointment is allowed only if the Building Authority is notified within 48 hours via Form BA10.
D. This concurrent appointment is allowed for deep foundation works provided the Authorized Signatory co-signs the daily safety check sheets.
questions.statutoryRef: Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code) Section 5 & PNRC 38
questions.rationale: Under the Code of Practice for Site Safety Supervision (SSPS Code), the functional streams of site safety supervision—namely the AP stream, the RSE/RGE stream, and the Registered Contractor (RC) stream—must remain completely independent. A Technically Competent Person (TCP) in the Contractor's stream is strictly barred from simultaneously undertaking any supervisory role or signing logbooks for the AP, RSE, or RGE streams, regardless of whether the individual holds professional qualifications matching the other streams.

questions.scenario: An RGBC erects a 3-storey temporary office and storage shed complex on a construction site. The temporary structure is 9.5 meters in height, is positioned 1.2 meters away from the site boundary adjoining an existing residential estate, and features external walls constructed of unrated combustible expanded polystyrene (EPS) core panels. No temporary building permit has been applied for under Part IX of the Building (Planning) Regulations.
options: A. The structure is fully exempt from the Building (Planning) Regulations because all temporary sheds inside active construction sites enjoy total statutory immunity.

B. The RGBC is in contravention of B(P)R Regulations 53 and 54, as temporary contractor sheds exceeding 2 storeys or 7m in height, or situated within 1.5m of a boundary, require prior permit and must satisfy non-combustibility standards.
C. The contractor shed only requires the endorsement of the Registered Safety Officer (RSO) under the Factories and Industrial Undertakings Ordinance.
D. Temporary contractor structures are regulated solely under the Fire Services Ordinance and do not fall under the statutory purview of the Building Authority.
questions.statutoryRef: Building (Planning) Regulations (Cap. 123F) Regulations 53, 54 & 55 & Buildings Ordinance Section 40(2B)
questions.rationale: Under Part IX (Regulations 53, 54, and 55) of the Building (Planning) Regulations (Cap. 123F), contractor sheds and temporary buildings are subject to strict statutory controls. A temporary contractor shed cannot exceed two storeys or 7m in height, must not be erected within 1.5m of any site boundary unless specific fire resistance requirements are met, and cannot use combustible material panels without express permission/permit from the Building Authority. Carrying out such works without compliance constitutes a statutory offence under BO Section 40(2B).
